key_insight: A single high-resolution turbulent snapshot contains enough repeated spatial structure to train a patch-based super-resolution model that reconstructs unseen flow fields at extreme scale factors.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a data-efficient route for turbulence modeling and CFD post-processing when full high-resolution training databases are unavailable.
method: Train a WDSR network only on overlapping patches from one high-resolution homogeneous isotropic turbulence realization.
Predict super-resolved patches for unseen fields and stitch them together with Hann-window-weighted overlap-add.
Compare against interpolation and against WDSR trained on 1, 25, 50, and 100 full snapshots.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful reconstruction at x32 and x64 with improved vortical structures, better high-wavenumber energy recovery, and stronger multiscale statistics than conventional interpolation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the strong spatial redundancy of homogeneous turbulence, so results may not transfer directly to strongly inhomogeneous or transient flows.
paper_title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
